# How deep the backlog is

**Generated by `scripts/build_backlog_depth.py`. Do not edit.**

Every outstanding machine-reading job, placed by the **meeting’s own date** — not by when we discovered it. 5,425 jobs, about $1,057, roughly 2.1 of a week’s allowance.

| stream | what one job is | jobs | $ each | $ total |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `votes` | the votes in the town’s minutes, with verbatim quotes | 3,081 | $0.09 | $265 |
| `reconcile` | our minutes of a recording against the town’s, one meeting | 228 | — | — |
| `minutes` | our minutes written from a recording’s captions | 2,116 | $0.37 | $792 |

**The streams are not interchangeable and must not be added into one bar.** `reconcile` can only exist where a recording exists, so its zero before 2025 is the channel’s start date, not neglect.

**THE MONEY ABOVE IS SHORT BY 228 JOB(S).** `reconcile` carries no measured cost, because `agentic-spend.csv` is written by `sweep_backlog.py` and that stream has only just been added — until today the daily refresh was the only thing that ran it, and the refresh does not price into that ledger. A dash is what an unmeasured cost looks like; the total is of the streams that have one, and it stops understating the first time the sweeper runs.

## What this does not say

- When any of this will be done. The sweep runs in whatever allowance is left before the weekly reset, which varies.
- That a zero is an absence. `reconcile` cannot exist before the recordings do, so its zero before 2025 is the channel’s start date and not a gap.
